title: Compact Smart Presets for Token Throttle & Prefix Cache
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design a compact, single-line 'Smart Presets' slate to let engineers and platform owners quickly apply recommended token-throttling and prefix-cache profiles. The slate targets two personas: (1) Product engineers who want low-effort cost reductions with predictable latency, and (2) Platform operators who need versionable presets for canary/rollout policies. The UI should fit within the route-level settings panel, support keyboard-first flows, show an inline cost delta estimate, and provide an explainable rationale chip that surfaces the telemetry signal that triggered the recommendation.
acceptance_criteria: Compact preset selector appears in route settings and is keyboard navigable
Selecting a preset updates the preview token latency / cost estimator in under 300ms
Rationale chip opens a lightweight modal with reproducible simulation inputs and a link to the eval run
Presets can be saved as named, versioned entries and appear in rollout policies for canary/AB
Accessibility: color contrast >= 4.5:1 for chips; all interactive controls reachable via screen reader and keyboard
design_notes: We intentionally avoid deep collapsible panels; the compact slate must be <= 96px high in collapsed form
Preset types: conservative (latency-safe), balanced (cost/latency trade), aggressive (cost-first). Each preset maps to batching window, max batch size, and prefix cache TTL and size limit
Rationale chip copies: 'Telemetry: 45% repeated prefixes | 95th latency headroom 120ms' — these are generated strings; we need a localization plan
Cost estimator uses route historical token distribution and current pricing table to show % delta and estimated $/1M tokens
Interaction: preview sim runs on client with cached shard of telemetry and falls back to server-side sim if input window is large
Security: presets do not expose raw customer data; simulation inputs must be anonymized and hashed
decisions: Show three default presets (conservative/balanced/aggressive) with 'Customize' inline affordance
Inline cost estimator shows both relative % and absolute $/1M tokens to aid cross-account comparisons
Presets are first-class config objects stored under 'presets' namespace and can be pinned to routes or global org settings
Simulations default to a 1-hour sample window; user can expand to 24h in the modal
tradeoffs: Compactness vs discoverability: collapsing detailed knobs may hide control from power users — mitigated with 'Customize' and keyboard shortcuts
Client-side quick sim is fast but less precise; server-side sim is accurate but costs compute — default to quick sim with opt-in full sim
Presenting monetary estimates risks confusion across regions with different pricing — include explicit currency and link to pricing page
next_steps: Design handoff: prepare tokens and component specs (buttons, chips, mini-estimator card)
UX research: 5 sessions with platform engineers and 5 sessions with product engineers to validate presets names and rationale text
Engineering spike: frontend perf budget to ensure preview sim completes in <300ms for common routes
Accessibility review: schedule with a11y engineer and test with VoiceOver and NVDA
Sync with runtime team to formalize the telemetry signals used by rationale (prefix-repeat-rate, kv-hit-rate, latency-headroom)
